title: Vary the learner's moves
statement: Give each interactive move in a course its own action, and never run three moves of one kind in a row, so the moves don't feel repetitive.
example: A static gate fails a course in which one verb is used twice or three moves of one kind come in a row.
detail: Review feedback on a 3D version of the Grade 9 lessons noted stage moves repeating across lessons, such as taking a mask off and putting it back (`othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, lines 8-9). Every move now needs a verb unique in the course, and a static gate fails the course when a verb is used twice or when three moves in a row in one lesson are of one kind, click, drag or choose (`othello-archive/src/scene/moments/kit.ts`, line 35; `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, lines 8 and 13).
against: The gate allows one deliberate pair, a mask taken off and put back, under a course budget of two mask moves (`othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, line 10).

evidence.quote: the same verb is used twice in the course
take mask, put mask across lessons
three moves in a row in one lesson of the same kind (click/drag/choose)
Make a move. Every move needs a course-unique `verb` (the variety gate checks it) and an `expect` (the vision gate).
more than 2 mask moves in the course (L1's take-off / put-back pair is the only one)
